title: Streetcar accident with Rene's band and the $30 bass settlement
summary: Dawson tells how a truck carrying Rene's band was hit by a streetcar and he alone accepted $30 for his smashed bass, around 1910.

story.theme_name: Life on the road: touring bands, buses and one-nighters
story.community_name: Life on the road: buses, trains and one-nighters

blocks.x: Were you in the band then?

I played, I was in the band when Morris French was playing Trombone with him. And, uh, when we had, uh, the time we made that time, uh, we had that accident, uh, on, uh, Dauphine and, say Rock I think. Dauphine, it was an Italian fella had, he had bought a truck and he didn't, he didn't know much about driving. Well, they had a car, a street car was running down Dauphine Street then. And when we got to, say, Rock and Dauphine, that's where the, uh, you bet with that accident he'd be frozen in the car, the truck on the track, and, uh, he didn't, he couldn't get the, the truck off the track quick enough for the car. The car came along and I jumped out the back of the, the truck. I hit my hip on the side, Morris French, he, he got his horn all busted. And René got his trumpet, uh, mashed, and my bassist got all grinded up in the, on the streetcar track. And, uh, so, well, René went and, uh, told me not to accept nothing, that he was gonna get a lawyer. And, uh, so I, same way, uh, I went to the public service and explained it to him and he showed me all the records and said, well, it's an interesting, and he faltered the driver, truck driver. And, uh, every, every seat of paper he turned over, the fella told me, he said, you know, I'm a old musician, fella at the public service. He said, now, he said, you valued your, uh, bass at $80, $85, that's what he said. Now, at that time on Ramport Street you could get second-handed basses, you see, had plenty of them. And he said, I know you can get a bass for $30 and a good one. So he said, uh, will you accept $30 for your bass? And I told him, yes, me. He gave me $30. Uh, René got sold with me, but I didn't care, but he, they wind up, none of them didn't get nothing for the answer, but he got all busted.

Yeah, me, I'm the only one who got $30. They got a lawyer and they tried to sue public service, and I knew they didn't have no chance, you know, with that public service. But I accepted the $30. And I went on Ramport Street and I got me old bass too. Cheaper than $30 too. I got a bass for $12. And I had that bass for a long time too.
Oh gee, that was way around, that was about, I think it was around 1910. That's around 1910 when I was with him.
Yeah. Before the big storm? Yeah.
Before that September storm. Yeah. Yes sir.
